media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static process-explainer poster.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/36.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered poster only, not the accuracy of its algorithm claims.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the oversized LinkedIn wordmark, app icon and highlighted year establish a timely platform subject. 3-10s: four numbered step cards make a hidden process feel finite and legible. 10-30s: the two bottom panels turn the explanation into an actionable reward-versus-punishment checklist.
creative.lived_work_moment: A creator is trying to decide what publishing behaviour is worth changing when platform distribution feels opaque.
creative.reader_payoff: A scan-friendly visual model for discussing a claimed distribution process and its practical implications; the statements themselves need separate verification.
creative.argument_sequence: Timely system headline -> four stated stages -> signals said to be rewarded -> signals said to be punished -> short operating response.
creative.utility: Reference sheet for a publishing conversation or a pre-posting checklist, contingent on independently checking its platform claims.
creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from an opaque system through apparent procedural clarity.
creative.transferable_atoms: Expose an invisible process through a small number of named stages. Use a final contrast panel to distinguish helpful and harmful responses. Keep process and response visually separate so the reader can skim either layer.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the LinkedIn icon treatment, exact 2026 headline, four stage labels, particular claims, red-green checklists, creator footer, or blue brand styling.

visual.composition: Tall white poster with a two-line headline, then a 2-by-2 grid of large rounded process cards, followed by two half-width bottom panels and a blue footer.
visual.hierarchy: The large black-and-blue headline dominates; blue step pills and panel titles create the second reading layer; bullets and miniature illustrations are tertiary.
visual.eye_path: Headline and app icon -> Step 1/2 row -> Step 3/4 row -> punishment/work-with contrast -> creator footer.
visual.imagery: A glossy LinkedIn app icon, tiny rule-sheet screenshots, check/cross badges and a concentric audience diagram act as explanatory anchors rather than decorative scenes.
visual.typography: Heavy rounded sans-serif title and section labels; smaller rounded sans bullets; blue step tags give the grid a repeated index.
visual.layout: A strict two-column board with repeated bordered cards, but the final two panels intentionally break the four-step rhythm to become an operational summary.
visual.pacing: Fast topical recognition, two short horizontal scans across the numbered cards, then a slower bottom comparison; density remains moderate because each panel has one job.
visual.technical_treatment: Off-white ground, black type, LinkedIn blue as the dominant accent, thin grey outlines, small green/red semantic markers and light drop shadows.
visual.visual_mechanism: A numbered grid converts a claimed back-end process into a visible sequence; the bottom comparison translates the model into behavioural choices.
visual.craft_notes: The title uses colour only on the platform name and a pale highlight only on the year, preserving entry focus. The central audience graphic earns its space by showing nested reach rather than repeating a bullet. Footer branding is visually separated from the educational body.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static two-sided operating comparison.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/33.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered comparison visual.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: two enormous opposing labels and a central VS spine make the comparison intelligible before individual words are read. 3-10s: the reader finds the shared category rail and can compare one row at a time. 10-30s: repeated rows surface the specific behaviour change implied by mature versus immature planning.
creative.lived_work_moment: A planning team needs language to distinguish reactive S&OP habits from more deliberate ways of working.
creative.reader_payoff: A meeting-ready diagnostic comparison that lets a reader name which operating behaviour is currently visible.
creative.argument_sequence: Opposed maturity labels -> shared decision categories -> row-by-row behavioural contrast -> invitation to assess the own operating model.
creative.utility: Saveable facilitation aid for discussing planning maturity without requiring a long explanatory article.
creative.emotional_trigger: Recognition and mild discomfort: readers can locate a familiar reactive habit on the left-hand side.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a comparison only when both sides answer the same categories. Let a central spine hold the shared dimensions so neither side has to repeat labels. Make the contrast a behavioural difference rather than a vague good-versus-bad adjective.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the Immature/Mature S&OP wording, orange-and-ochre headers, central charcoal spine, exact category set, photo/footer, or the source's conclusions.

visual.composition: Full-height two-column comparison: an orange left lane and ochre right lane flank a wide dark charcoal central spine that carries seven category labels.
visual.hierarchy: The two giant opposing headers and VS badge dominate, then the central category labels, then each paired sentence.
visual.eye_path: Left and right headers -> VS spine -> one horizontal category row at a time from Variability to Alignment -> dark footer.
visual.imagery: Minimal icons live inside the central spine; the comparative table is the visual proof rather than a decorative illustration.
visual.typography: Condensed all-caps display type for major labels; large black sans for each side's claims; central labels are white, all-caps and vertically stacked.
visual.layout: A symmetrical matrix with rows aligned precisely across both columns. The central spine absorbs the labels so the two outer lanes can devote full width to the contrast.
visual.pacing: Immediate binary framing, then a disciplined vertical reading rhythm. Repeated row height makes a dense comparison feel navigable.
visual.technical_treatment: Very high contrast: flat white cards, strong charcoal divider, warm maturity colours, narrow coloured row rules and a full-width dark CTA footer.
visual.visual_mechanism: The shared spine proves that both sides are being judged against identical operating dimensions, making the side-by-side contrast feel like a diagnosis rather than a list.
visual.craft_notes: The mid-column is sufficiently wide to prevent category labels becoming footnotes. Consistent row alignment prevents false comparisons. Colour marks sides and is not used as an extra data variable.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static five-level maturity-pyramid poster.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/29.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered hierarchy and its visible text.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the massive five-level title and rainbow pyramid promise a finite maturity model. 3-10s: the eye climbs the stepped central object from foundational to strategic. 10-30s: leadership actions in the lower boxes turn the hierarchy into a reference sheet.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement or transformation leader needs a simple way to discuss whether AI ambition is ahead of operational readiness.
creative.reader_payoff: A visually memorable maturity conversation starter with a clearly ordered framework; its claims and prescribed levels need independent validation before use as advice.
creative.argument_sequence: Five-level promise -> central ordered stack -> level-specific annotations -> leadership action boxes -> branded invitation.
creative.utility: A saveable orientation model for initiating a maturity discussion, not a substitute for an assessment method.
creative.emotional_trigger: Ambition tempered by the visible warning that upper levels depend on lower foundations.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a spatial hierarchy when the relationship genuinely is dependency or sequence. Add a separate action zone only after the hierarchy is clear. Let colour separate levels but preserve a single reading direction.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the exact five-level procurement AI model, pyramid geometry, colour sequence, leadership boxes, quote treatment, source wording, portrait or Supply Chain AI Pro branding.

visual.composition: Tall parchment-toned poster: oversized editorial title across the top, central five-step 3D pyramid, quotation box at upper left, explanatory note at upper right, and five compact action boxes along the lower third.
visual.hierarchy: Title first, pyramid second, level labels third; supporting callouts and lower action boxes are close-read material.
visual.eye_path: Title -> green pyramid tip -> descending coloured levels -> bottom leadership strategy heading -> five coloured action boxes -> footer.
visual.imagery: The pyramid is the primary explanatory object. Quote punctuation, a small portrait and brand devices are secondary framing elements.
visual.typography: Bold serif title, broad rounded sans level labels, oblique/slanted text on pyramid faces, compact sans supporting copy, and all-caps action-box headings.
visual.layout: A central symmetric hierarchy floats in a field of off-white texture. Auxiliary content fills the left, right and lower margins without challenging the pyramid's dominance.
visual.pacing: Fast vertical orientation at thumbnail size, then a more demanding read of angled labels and small text. The lower action blocks create a second, optional reading pass.
visual.technical_treatment: Paper texture, black typography, saturated pastel-rainbow level planes, black line emphasis and a gold brand footer; 3D facets make the hierarchy feel physical.
visual.visual_mechanism: The shrinking stacked form encodes progression and dependency: readers understand the base-to-tip relation before they parse the language.
visual.craft_notes: The central object carries the argument but some supporting text is dense for feed use. Diagonal labels use the pyramid's face angle, helping integration but reducing scan speed. The secondary boxes are visually separated so they do not look like extra pyramid levels.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static concentric-layer operations poster.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/26.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered poster and its visible layers.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the headline, industrial sketch environment and turquoise core immediately frame a layered Lean operation. 3-10s: the dotted Start here route leads into Standard Work at the centre. 10-30s: concentric rings make the prerequisite logic and small supporting practices inspectable.
creative.lived_work_moment: An operations leader is deciding where to start when improvement activity, management routines and culture are being discussed at the same time.
creative.reader_payoff: A memorable visual way to discuss a proposed order of operating layers; the framework remains a point of view rather than a universal maturity model.
creative.argument_sequence: Layer-count promise -> Start here pointer -> central Standard Work -> expanding management and culture layers -> illustrative practices around each ring.
creative.utility: A workshop prompt or a saveable way to introduce a dependency conversation in continuous improvement.
creative.emotional_trigger: Order replacing improvement overload: the visual offers a clear starting point within a complex factory setting.
creative.transferable_atoms: When a framework has prerequisites, locate the starting condition physically at the centre and make later layers radiate outward. Use an environmental scene only if it reinforces the work context. Give the reader a directional cue rather than assuming concentric rings alone explain priority.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the factory line-art scene, five named Lean layers, turquoise standard-work centre, exact dotted path, handwritten Before/After labels, or source wording.

visual.composition: Square editorial poster: a large centred concentric target occupies the middle while detailed monochrome factory line art frames the outer edges; a turquoise handwritten route enters from upper left.
visual.hierarchy: The large LEAN OPERATION title and turquoise Standard Work core dominate; ring labels follow; small practice labels and factory detail form the close-read layer.
visual.eye_path: Headline -> turquoise Start here cue -> dotted route -> Standard Work core -> rings moving outward -> Before/After labels at the bottom corners.
visual.imagery: The factory is a contextual frame, while the concentric diagram is the functional visual. The rough turquoise centre gives the abstract core a tactile mark.
visual.typography: Tall condensed navy display headline, all-caps ring labels, small condensed explanatory labels, plus a contrasting loose handwritten script for directional emphasis.
visual.layout: A central circular diagram owns the page; outer industrial drawing is deliberately lower contrast so it suggests context without obscuring the rings.
visual.pacing: The route provides an immediate entry. Readers can then move ring by ring, with side labels rewarding a slower exploration.
visual.technical_treatment: Off-white paper, fine navy sketch lines, turquoise brush accents, restrained shadows and a mixture of clean vector rings with hand-rendered texture.
visual.visual_mechanism: The concentric structure makes foundational-to-cultural dependency spatial, while the entry arrow prevents readers from treating outer layers as an interchangeable list.
visual.craft_notes: The environmental illustration is unusually integrated: it supports the topic without becoming a stock hero. Turquoise is reserved for the central proof point and path. The close-read labels are dispersed around the ring circumference, encouraging exploration rather than a simple top-to-bottom scan.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static multi-framework strategy library poster.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/19'.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered library of mini-graphics.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the enormous Strategy Book in One Page headline promises unusually high value density. 3-10s: a mosaic of recognisably different diagrams signals breadth and makes readers search for a familiar framework. 10-30s: the reader can zoom into one mini-framework at a time and return later for the rest.
creative.lived_work_moment: A strategy practitioner wants a compact index of common planning frameworks instead of a single long article.
creative.reader_payoff: A browsable visual library that aids recall and gives multiple entry points; individual framework claims need their own source checking.
creative.argument_sequence: One-page library promise -> many named mini-frameworks -> varied diagrams and checklists -> free-download CTA.
creative.utility: High save potential as an index or memory jogger, with value accumulating across repeat visits.
creative.emotional_trigger: Abundance and competence: the reader is offered a whole shelf of familiar tools in one visual.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a true reference library, use a stable page title and a deliberately varied set of diagram primitives. Give each module enough local completion to be useful but avoid pretending the mosaic is one linear argument. Build a navigable visual index rather than repeating identical cards.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the Strategy Book title, particular framework selection, Eric Partaker mini-diagrams, paper texture, gold corner tabs, blue footer or collection layout.

visual.composition: Tall off-white editorial sheet headed by a large serif title, then a dense four-column mosaic of roughly a dozen different strategy mini-diagrams, with a full-width blue download footer.
visual.hierarchy: The huge title is the sole thumbnail-level anchor; at normal size each named mini-framework competes as a local entry point; fine print lives inside each tile.
visual.eye_path: Title -> whichever mini-framework catches the reader's eye -> adjacent diagrams by local colour or geometry -> blue footer. There is no required single reading order.
visual.imagery: Each module uses its own diagram primitive: tables, wheels, matrices, staircases, loops, a skyline, Venn-style circles and small people illustrations.
visual.typography: Editorial serif for headings, compact sans for body copy, varied subhead sizes; labels are bold enough to act as a browsing index.
visual.layout: A deliberately packed magazine-like grid with unequal module sizes. Thin white gutters and colour blocks prevent the sheet from collapsing into an undifferentiated wall.
visual.pacing: The title is immediate; next comes exploratory browsing rather than a sequential lesson. The image rewards multiple 10-30 second visits.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm paper texture, black editorial type, restrained pastel blocks, thin line diagrams, occasional bold primary colours and small gold tape-like corner accents.
visual.visual_mechanism: The mosaic is a catalogue mechanism: visual variety helps a reader locate and remember a framework by shape as well as title.
visual.craft_notes: The density is earned by genuine variation in information form, not by duplicating one card treatment. Some microtext is too small for a feed preview but works as a reason to save. Module boundaries are clear even though the entire page has an intentionally library-like abundance.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 GIF: a three-column content-prompt reference sheet with small marker movement.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Direct inspection of references/top 100/27.gif against the declared SHA-256, including frame 0, 87 and 174. The analysis describes its visible sheet and restrained marker animation.

gif_frame_evidence.observation: Complete three-column sheet is already readable: Life, Expertise and Business buckets sit above five prompt cards each, connected by thin vertical rails.
The static reference sheet remains intact while small coloured teardrop markers appear at different positions on the rails, directing attention down the content buckets.
The finished sheet returns to the full title-and-three-bucket composition; the prompt inventory remains the durable information layer, not the animation.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: an oversized orange frequency promise answers a familiar creator problem. 3-10s: three pastel buckets establish a simple content taxonomy. 10-30s: the reader hunts through five prompt patterns in each bucket and can save the sheet as a reusable idea bank.
creative.lived_work_moment: A creator wants enough distinct prompt starters to maintain a regular posting rhythm without repeatedly beginning from a blank page.
creative.reader_payoff: A browsable collection of prompt frameworks organised by content role rather than a vague injunction to post more.
creative.argument_sequence: Posting-frequency tension -> three content buckets -> stated ratio and audience response for each -> five starter patterns per bucket.
creative.utility: A repeat-use prompt inventory that encourages return visits while planning a week of content.
creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from idea scarcity plus confidence that different post types can serve different reader reactions.
creative.transferable_atoms: Divide a repeatable content system by genuinely different roles, then let each role contain reusable prompts. Use high density only when every cell is independently selectable. Animate an attention path or state change, not the explanatory text itself.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the exact five-times-a-week promise, Life/Expertise/Business labels, the content ratios, individual prompt formulas, lavender-mint-pink column treatment, teardrop animation or source branding.

visual.composition: Tall warm-off-white sheet: oversized orange headline and one-line instruction above three evenly spaced tapered columns, each with a tinted category header, a short specification block and five vertically linked prompt cards.
visual.hierarchy: Headline first; Life, Expertise and Business headers second; card titles third; card copy is close-read material.
visual.eye_path: Orange title -> three coloured category headers -> short category instruction rows -> connected prompt cards within one chosen column -> adjacent column comparison.
visual.imagery: No illustrative scene is needed. The tapered containers, rails and moving coloured droplets act as the diagrammatic imagery.
visual.typography: Very large heavy orange sans title; bold black category and card titles; compact sans body; repeated section labels create a worksheet feel.
visual.layout: A highly regular three-column comparison/reference sheet. Each column uses the same vertical grammar but contains a different role and different prompt templates.
visual.pacing: The static layout gives an immediate taxonomy, then supports a deep, non-linear scan. The GIF adds mild motion without changing the visual's informational contract.
visual.technical_treatment: Pale peach ground, black typography, orange headline, lavender/mint/pink category fields, rounded black outlines, modest shadows and thin connector rails.
visual.visual_mechanism: Parallel labelled buckets make a content mix visible; the repeated card stacks turn a vague planning goal into a menu of selectable starting points.
visual.craft_notes: The tapering buckets signal containment and categorisation without a generic dashboard feel. Motion is intentionally subservient: the moving markers are a scan cue, while the final/first frame remains useful as a static graphic. Cards are readable because each rail has ample vertical spacing.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static, category-and-logo tool directory.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/17.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered directory visual.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: a large numerical promise and the Claude mark announce an exhaustive tool list. 3-10s: soft coloured category containers make the catalogue scannable by use case. 10-30s: app logos and short action descriptions reward readers who search for the relevant workflow category.
creative.lived_work_moment: A practitioner is looking for integrations but does not know which adjacent systems could connect to a chosen AI environment.
creative.reader_payoff: A compact browsing directory organised by the work outcome an integration supports, rather than a raw logo dump.
creative.argument_sequence: Numbered directory promise -> category headers with short utility statement -> recognizable app logos -> three-step setup strip.
creative.utility: Reference list for return visits when a reader later needs a tool in a particular operational category.
creative.emotional_trigger: Possibility and control: a scattered software landscape is made to feel navigable.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a tool directory, group items by the job they enable and give each group a concrete one-line outcome. Use recognisable marks as retrieval anchors but do not let logos replace the organizing logic. End with the smallest viable start path.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the exact 34-server list, Claude/Zapier wording, app logos, pastel category boxes, three-step setup strip, Charlie Hills footer or source typography.

visual.composition: Tall white directory with a two-line navy headline, nine rounded category containers of different sizes, rows of app logo tiles, and a full-width dark-navy three-step footer.
visual.hierarchy: The large Top 34 headline dominates; coloured category label pills and group titles lead the second scan; logos and app names support recognition.
visual.eye_path: Headline -> subtitle -> large social category -> neighbouring category blocks by colour -> bottom three-step strip -> footer brand.
visual.imagery: Logo tiles are functional imagery, acting as fast-recognition markers inside each category. No scene illustration competes with the directory.
visual.typography: Clean rounded sans for headline and instructions; compact all-caps category labels; small app names below oversized logo marks.
visual.layout: A modular grid that varies block width according to category size while maintaining common inner spacing. The first category spans the full width, then later categories form two- and three-column bands.
visual.pacing: Immediate count and platform association; readers then browse only the relevant category. The footer gives a slower, ordered next step after the non-linear directory scan.
visual.technical_treatment: White ground, deep navy type, pale blue/purple/orange/mint/yellow/lime/pink outlines and fills, rounded cards, light borders and crisp logo tiles.
visual.visual_mechanism: Categorical grouping tames a long inventory: colour, label and logos cooperate to make a reader find an app by functional destination.
visual.craft_notes: The visual is dense but has a stable unit: group title, one-line outcome, logo grid. Category size is encoded by container area rather than a misleading quantitative chart. The dark setup strip deliberately closes the page with a different reading mode.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static 20-row procurement use-case matrix.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/22.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered matrix and visible density.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the large 20 Procurement AI Use Cases headline promises a finite, role-specific reference. 3-10s: the table headers reveal a useful schema of use case, prompt, inputs, format and outcome. 10-30s: the reader finds one job row and can inspect its input/output contract.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement practitioner needs specific, bounded ways to turn an AI discussion into a possible task, input and output.
creative.reader_payoff: A dense discovery matrix that translates broad AI interest into named procurement work patterns, subject to review of its stated prompts and outcomes.
creative.argument_sequence: Counted use-case promise -> five-column operating schema -> twenty task rows -> product/author footer.
creative.utility: A reference to revisit while selecting one procurement workflow to investigate or prototype.
creative.emotional_trigger: Practical possibility: broad AI language is converted into a list of recognisable procurement tasks.
creative.transferable_atoms: When presenting many use cases, choose a fixed schema that includes the actual input and expected output rather than only a benefit. Make the first column a scan index. Use density only when a reader can extract a row without needing the entire table.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the exact 20 procurement use cases, prompt text, five-column matrix, pastel row labels, Supply Chain AI Pro branding, portrait or footer treatment.

visual.composition: Very tall white portrait matrix: a large navy title above a five-column table with a dark navy header row, twenty ruled rows, and a black-and-gold branded footer.
visual.hierarchy: The quantity-and-topic title provides entry; dark column headers establish the data schema; coloured use-case labels form the scrollable index; smaller prompt and outcome text supplies detail.
visual.eye_path: Headline -> table headers -> left use-case column -> across a selected row from prompt to inputs, format and outcome -> branded footer.
visual.imagery: There is almost no pictorial imagery; colour-coded use-case name cells carry the visual indexing function.
visual.typography: Heavy navy sans headline, white all-caps table headers, bold coloured use-case labels and smaller compact body text with italicised prompt language.
visual.layout: A strict spreadsheet-like grid of five unequal columns. Wide prompt/input/outcome columns accommodate detailed prose, while the narrow use-case column supports scanning.
visual.pacing: Fast schema recognition, then a slow row-level reference read. The format intentionally privileges saving and zooming over instant casual consumption.
visual.technical_treatment: White ground, dark navy table header and footer, light grey cell rules, alternating soft pastel use-case label pills and a gold footer band.
visual.visual_mechanism: The repeated input-to-outcome row structure makes each AI idea feel operationally bounded instead of generic; table form itself supplies credibility and retrieval.
visual.craft_notes: The matrix earns its density because all five columns answer different practical questions. Most body copy is too small for feed-speed reading, making the title and schema essential. Colour appears only in the first-column labels, avoiding a false data encoding.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static three-way terminology comparison.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/24.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered comparison sheet.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: three giant labels separated by bold VS bars signal a terminology distinction. 3-10s: the repeated What is it / When to use / How they guide you / Best practices / Common mistakes structure promises comparable answers. 10-30s: readers can stay in one column or compare the final relationship band.
creative.lived_work_moment: A manager or team needs to stop conflating goals, performance measures and critical success factors during planning or performance conversations.
creative.reader_payoff: A common-schema comparison that clarifies the different jobs of three familiar management terms.
creative.argument_sequence: Three-way label contrast -> repeated definitions and use cases -> pitfalls -> shared lower explanation of how the terms work together.
creative.utility: Onboarding or meeting reference when a team needs shared vocabulary across planning and measurement.
creative.emotional_trigger: Clarity and reduced confusion around words that are often used interchangeably.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a three-way distinction, make each column answer exactly the same questions. Use a final integration strip only after the differences are clear. Give each concept a distinct colour field, but retain one shared typographic grid.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the OKR/KPI/CSF wording, three-column colour palette, exact comparison categories, line-icon set, final circle relationship graphic, Eric Partaker credit or footer.

visual.composition: Tall paper-toned sheet with a giant three-term headline, followed by three full-height pastel columns and one bottom integration band spanning the width.
visual.hierarchy: The three giant terms dominate first; all-caps column labels and line icons lead next; question prompts and bold subheads structure the close-read copy.
visual.eye_path: Top title -> one chosen column from icon to examples -> neighbouring columns for contrast -> full-width How they work together band -> blue footer.
visual.imagery: Simple black line icons inside each column represent each category; the small linked circles in the lower band provide the only relationship diagram.
visual.typography: Large editorial serif for the title, heavy black sans for columns/subheads, compact sans body and modest use of bold in the examples.
visual.layout: Three equal vertical lanes use an identical sequence of sections and baselines. A bottom panel breaks the columns to explain the relationship across them.
visual.pacing: The structure is highly predictable: instant three-way frame, then column-level deep read, then integration. Readers can enter non-linearly without losing context.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm off-white paper, pale blue/yellow/pink fields, thin matching colour outlines, black type, small black line icons and a saturated blue newsletter footer.
visual.visual_mechanism: Equal columns prevent the concepts from collapsing into one blended list; the lower band repairs the separation by showing how they connect.
visual.craft_notes: The comparison grammar is stronger than the decorative texture. The oversized title makes the long poster legible in a feed. The bottom relationship strip is important: without it, the visual would risk presenting related planning terms as isolated silos.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static seven-module outreach cheat-sheet.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer - Batch C
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/21.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the rendered dark, modular cheat-sheet.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0-3s: the large LinkedIn Outreach 2026 title, dark field and Cheat Sheet label make the page feel like a premium reference object. 3-10s: seven large numbered module titles form a contents map. 10-30s: coloured panels let a reader jump to principles, campaign structure, copy examples, metrics or tech stack.
creative.lived_work_moment: A commercial practitioner is assembling an outreach system and wants one page that names the moving parts.
creative.reader_payoff: A visually indexed working sheet that gathers several outreach decisions in one place; stated benchmarks and practices need their own evidence check.
creative.argument_sequence: Time-stamped cheat-sheet promise -> seven named operating modules -> examples/metrics/tool stack -> closing rule and brand strip.
creative.utility: Return-value reference: readers can revisit a single coloured module when a relevant campaign decision arises.
creative.emotional_trigger: Control over a complex multi-step workflow, reinforced by a polished technical interface feel.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a multi-part operating guide, use large numbered modules as a navigation system and let each module use the diagram type that best fits its job. A dark field can support density if type, borders and semantic colours retain high contrast. Do not mistake glowing panels for proof.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the LinkedIn Outreach title, claimed benchmarks, seven-module content, dark starfield/grid treatment, rainbow panel palette, source portraits, company logo or specific outreach advice.

visual.composition: Tall near-black poster with a large title, then seven rounded modules arranged as one full-width top band, two medium second-row blocks, three equal third-row blocks and a full-width concluding band.
visual.hierarchy: Title and Cheat Sheet capsule are largest; numbered module headings are second; glowing borders and coloured panels create the scan map; tables and microcopy are close-read.
visual.eye_path: Title -> red Principles band -> amber Campaign and olive Copy modules -> green Metrics, cyan Tech Stack and purple People tiles -> magenta final rule -> footer.
visual.imagery: Small portrait circles, app icons and compact interface/table shapes supply examples; the main imagery is the board-like system of coloured modules.
visual.typography: Bold white sans headings, compact muted grey microcopy, white table labels and colour-highlighted metrics/keywords. Module numbers sit in filled rounded squares.
visual.layout: A dashboard-like but deliberately editorial modular grid. Modules vary in height and width according to their information form, while retaining common rounded corners and perimeter spacing.
visual.pacing: Immediate premium cheat-sheet impression; readers browse by colour and module title, then slow down inside one panel. The final band works as a memorable close.

visual.typography: Editorial serif headline, heavy black sans module titles, bold Use For labels, compact explanatory copy and white numerals in coloured circular badges.
visual.layout: A deliberately varied grid: three narrow modules at top, a medium left module, a wide central module, and two large lower modules. All keep a common rounded rectangle and coloured-outline family.
visual.pacing: Immediate library promise, quick recognition through module titles/shapes, then non-linear deep inspection of one framework. The page is designed for repeated browsing rather than a single narrative read.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm white paper, black type, pale blue/mint/yellow/peach/aqua/pink/lavender module fields, matching thin borders, bright number discs and a saturated blue footer strip.
visual.visual_mechanism: The mosaic makes selection visual: framework names, local diagram shapes and use conditions act together as an index for different decision contexts.
visual.craft_notes: Module geometry varies with content rather than merely decoration, which keeps high density cognitively organised. The broad central SPADE panel anchors the composition while top/bottom rows retain balance. Consistent rounded frames and number discs keep the library unified despite different diagram forms.
